leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open. The negative balance created by the Conte purchase was closed by the Amoako sale, and the arithmetic reconciles exactly against the prior run's figure. The balance is positive and there are almost six days to the matchday 3 lock, so there is no unwind deadline pressure of any kind. The standing danger is the reverse: because the safe ceiling now depends on a single sale, and because a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the whole matchday, any buy above the ceiling would re-open leverage that the one permitted sale cannot close. That is precisely why the only attractive target on the board was declined.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is squad size, not money and not any single position. At exactly eleven players there is one legal formation, no bench, and no cover: if any single player picks up a knock or a suspension before the matchday 3 lock, he cannot be replaced without a buy, and the buy must land before any sale or the missing-player penalty applies. That is the exposure to watch over the next six days. The weakest fielded slots are the two designated sales — the right-back who is not starting and the midfielder whose average is far below the rest of the eleven — and upgrading either requires a buy that lands first and still leaves the balance non-negative at the lock. Only one candidate on the board would genuinely improve the eleven, and he is priced just out of reach.

verdict.detail: No action needed, and for once that is a clean answer rather than a quiet market. The Conte-for-Amoako cycle completed while you were away: Amoako sold to Kickbase at exactly mv, the negative balance is gone, and the books reconcile to the cent. That leaves the squad sitting exactly on the eleven-man floor with one legal formation and no bench at all. There is nothing to buy that clears both the points test and the money test, and there is nothing you can safely sell — so the right move is to leave it alone until matchday 2 finishes.

sell.reason: No sale is recommended, and there is a hard reason beyond the eleven-man floor. Matchday 2 is not finished. Five of the eleven have yet to play their locked fixture, and both of the only two sellable bodies — Lokonga and Widmer — are among them, with Lokonga in his club's probable XI. Selling either before those matches kick off forfeits live points from an eleven that is already locked. Widmer remains the standing designated sale on merit: dated club sources confirm he has made no starts this season and sits behind three others at right back. Lokonga stays a quality-based sale candidate, not an availability one — he is fit and starting. Neither should move before matchday 2 completes.

standing.name: Amoako
standing.why: THE UNWIND. This is the pre-priced second leg of the Conte trade and it is now due. Conte (3204) settled to Georg Kitz 2026-09-05T12:52:14Z at 12.000.000 against mv 9.292.405 = +29,14%, exactly the Brncinm call, and the balance is now -566.376. Selling Amoako to Kickbase at mv 1.569.143 puts it at +1.002.767 and closes the leveraged position outright. REVERSES AND CLOSES Hjmhal7, WHICH SAID DO NOT SELL HIM - say that out loud to Georg. Hjmhal7 was right on its own premise and the premise is dead: it protected Amoako as the ELEVENTH BODY of an 11-man squad, where selling him meant 10 players and the -100 penalty. Conte makes the squad TWELVE, so Amoako is now the twelfth body and the sale is free. POINTS COST ZERO, MEASURED: Amoako has no ap field at all (0 points, 0 minutes, 0 apps, 2x unused sub per Ligainsider 05.09.2026), so he leaves the fielded eleven at 12 players anyway. Squad after the sale is 11 = 1GK/4DEF/3MID/3ATT, which IS 4-3-3 exactly, legal, fully placed, fielded points 1439. HE IS THE RIGHT BODY AND THE ALTERNATIVE IS MEASURED: selling Widmer instead (mv 1.852.587, +283.444 more cash) forces 3-4-3 and costs 29 fielded points; selling Lokonga (mv 9.731.816) forces Amoako back into the eleven and costs 44. Amoako is the only points-free sale on the books. TIMING - SELL BEFORE 20:00Z: market values tick at 2026-09-05T20:00:00Z (mvud, first-party) and Amoako is decaying hard - tfhmvt -49.393, sdmvt -811.827 - so every tick he is held costs ~50k of unwind. There is no matchday risk forcing the hand (MD3 locks 2026-09-11T18:30Z, ~149,6h away, and MD2's lock passed 04.09 18:30Z with the balance still at +11.433.624, so no scored matchday has ever seen the negative), but there is no reason on earth to wait either. AFTER THIS THE SQUAD IS AT 11 AND FULLY INVESTED: cash ~1,00M, zero further sales possible without triggering -100, so the usable buy ceiling is ~1,00M and nothing on the board is reachable. That is the correct state, not a problem to solve.

buy.reason: Nothing to buy. The board threw up its most tempting shape of the week and it still fails. Cole Campbell has been relisted by a rival, and he is the genuine article: dated sources confirm he is fit, has started every game, played the large majority of available minutes, and his scoring average is a real full-match figure rather than a cameo artifact. Against Lokonga he would be the single largest points upgrade available anywhere on the board. He fails purely on arithmetic — the ask sits above the safe ceiling, and buying at it would leave the balance negative at the matchday lock, which scores zero for the entire matchday. Two buys and two sales do not rescue it either, because the second body would have to cost less than the league's minimum price. He is logged as a watch with a price trigger, not chased. Van den Bosch is the other one worth recording: honestly priced in the low cluster and a real upgrade on the weakest defensive slot, but a defender can only be unwound against Widmer, and that lever is far too small. Everything else on the board is either unaffordable by a wide margin, carries a high-cluster premium on a manager ask, or has no points record at all. Skarke deserves a specific note: his eye-catching average was independently confirmed today to be one goal in a single substitute cameo, with no starts all season — the reverse trap in its purest form.

fitness.sweep: The squad sweep is clean and dated. Every player returns no injury or suspension flag, none appears in the league's current injured-and-suspended table, and dated club sources place nine of the eleven in their current starting elevens. Two negatives, neither of them new and neither actionable. Widmer is confirmed a backup rather than a fringe starter — no starts, a handful of substitute minutes, behind three others in his position. He is fit, not suspended, and named to his club's Champions League squad, so there is no exit risk — it is a selection call. Crucially, nothing can be done about it: he is in the locked matchday 2 eleven, and at the eleven-man floor he cannot be sold. Tonight's kickoff settles it first-hand, which is a better basis for the next run than another projection.
